title: Queen Checkmate
description: Checkmate the lone king with your king and queen. The most important basic mate — you should be able to do it in under 10 moves.
hint: Place the queen a knight's move away from the enemy king to box it in, then bring your own king up.
technique: Shrink the king's box with the queen (a knight's move away mirrors it)
Push the king to the edge
Bring your king close — the queen can't mate alone
Always leave the king a legal move until the mate (no stalemate!)
pitfall: Watch out for stalemate: until the final check, always leave the black king a square to move to.

lesson.text: The queen can't mate on her own. First use her to **shrink the box** the black king lives in.
Then bring your king up. The mate comes on the edge, with the queen **protected by your king**.
The big trap is **stalemate**: here Black has no legal move and is not in check — it's a draw!

title: Queen Mate from the Centre
description: The black king starts in the middle of the board. Drive it to the edge and mate it.
hint: Qf6! takes away a whole block of squares at once.
technique: Restrict the king with the queen first
Walk the king towards the edge
Mate with the queen protected by the king
pitfall: Too slow or stalemate. Keep the queen a knight's jump from the king and bring your own king to help.

lesson.text: **Qf6!** takes the 6th rank and the f-file at once. The black king is locked in a smaller box.
Keep shrinking the box with quiet queen moves, then walk your king over to deliver mate on the edge.

title: Rook Checkmate
description: Checkmate the lone king with king and rook. The king must help, and the opposition is the key.
hint: Cut the king off with your rook along a rank, then bring your king up to face the enemy king.
technique: Cut the king off along a rank or file
Bring your king to face the enemy king (opposition)
Check along the edge when the kings face each other
Use a waiting rook move to gain the opposition
pitfall: The rook alone can't mate. Cut the king off, bring your king to face it, and check only when the kings stand face to face.

lesson.text: **Ra7!** cuts the black king off on the back rank. It can never come back.
Now walk your king up until it faces the black king. With the kings face to face, a rook check on the edge is **mate**.

title: Rook Mate from the Centre
description: A harder version: the enemy king is centralised. Box it in step by step.
hint: Start with Rh4 or Rh5 to cut the king off, then approach with your king.
technique: Make the box smaller with every rook move
Protect the rook with your king when it is attacked
Opposition + check on the edge = mate
pitfall: The box didn't get smaller. Each rook move should take away a rank or file, and keep the rook away from the black king.

lesson.text: Start by cutting the king off: **Rh4** keeps it above the 4th rank.
Bring your king up. When the kings face each other, check; otherwise make the box one row smaller.

title: Two Rooks: The Ladder
description: With two rooks you don't even need your king. Walk the enemy king to the edge like climbing a ladder.
hint: One rook cuts off a rank, the other checks on the next rank. Keep the rooks far from the king.
technique: Rook 1 cuts off a rank
Rook 2 gives check on the next rank
Leapfrog until the king reaches the edge
If the king attacks a rook, move it to the far side of the board
pitfall: A rook got too close to the king. If the king attacks a rook, swing it to the far side of the board.

lesson.text: One rook guards a rank, the other checks on the next one: **Rh4**, then **Ra5+**.
Keep climbing the ladder until the king reaches the edge — then it's mate.

title: Two Bishops Checkmate
description: Two bishops side by side form a wall the king can't cross. Drive it into a corner and mate.
hint: Place the bishops next to each other in the centre and use your king to push the enemy king back.
technique: Bishops side by side make an impassable diagonal wall
The king helps to take away squares
Drive the king to a corner
Watch out for stalemate in the corner
pitfall: The king escaped from the corner area or it was stalemate. Keep the bishops side by side and use your king to push.

lesson.text: Bishops side by side form a **diagonal wall** the king cannot cross.
Use your king to drive the enemy king into a corner. The final picture looks like this.

title: Bishop and Knight Checkmate
description: The hardest basic mate: it can take up to 33 moves. You can only force mate in a corner of the **bishop's colour** (a8 or h1 here).
hint: First push the king to the edge, then use the 'W manoeuvre' with the knight to drive it to a light corner.
technique: Centralise all three pieces
Drive the king to the edge
If it runs to the wrong (dark) corner, use the knight's W manoeuvre
Mate in the corner of the bishop's colour (a8 or h1)
pitfall: You can only force mate in a corner of the bishop's colour. Drive the king there with the knight's W manoeuvre — and be quick, the 50-move rule is watching.

lesson.text: First centralise all three pieces and push the black king towards the edge.
Mate is only possible in a corner of the **bishop's colour** — here a8 or h1 (light squares).
If the king runs to a wrong (dark) corner, the knight's **W manoeuvre** chases it along the edge to the right one.

title: Queen vs Rook
description: Queen against rook is a win, but the technique is demanding. Win the rook with a fork or force mate.
hint: Aim for the Philidor position: put the defending side in zugzwang so the rook must separate from its king.
technique: Keep your king close to the enemy king
Use zugzwang: make a waiting queen move
Once the rook leaves the king, look for a queen fork (check + rook)
pitfall: The rook kept checking or set up a stalemate trick. Keep your king close and wait for the rook to leave its king.

lesson.text: The rook is glued to its king. Use checks and **waiting queen moves** until Black has to move and the rook must step away.
Once the rook separates from its king, look for a **check that forks** king and rook.

title: King and Pawn: Key Squares
description: Promote your pawn. With your king in front of the pawn on the 5th rank, you can always reach a key square.
hint: Play Kd6 or Kf6: the king in front of the pawn wins.
technique: King in front of the pawn, not behind it
Reach a key square (d6, e6 or f6)
Use the opposition when the kings meet
pitfall: The black king got in front of your pawn with the opposition — that's a draw. Keep your king ahead of the pawn and reach a key square first.

lesson.text: **Key squares**: if your king reaches d6, e6 or f6, the pawn promotes no matter what Black does.
King first, pawn second: push the pawn only when your king has cleared the way.

title: Taking the Opposition
description: Only one move wins. Take the opposition and escort the pawn.
hint: Ke3! — face the black king with one square between the kings.
technique: Kings on the same file with one square between = opposition
The side that does NOT have to move has the opposition
Outflank: when the enemy king steps aside, move forward on the other side
pitfall: You lost the opposition: the black king stood in front of yours with you to move, and it blocked the pawn.

lesson.text: **Opposition**: kings facing each other with one square between them. The side that does *not* have to move wins the standoff.
After **Ke3** Black must give way, and your king walks to a key square: d4, e4 or f4.

title: King on the Sixth Rank
description: Your king is beside its pawn. One move wins, the others draw.
hint: Kb6 — the king in front of the pawn on the 6th rank always wins.
technique: King on the 6th rank in front of the pawn wins regardless of the opposition
Then push the pawn with the king's support
pitfall: Pushing the pawn too early lets the black king block it. King first, pawn second.

lesson.text: With your king on the 6th rank **in front of** the pawn, it always wins — whoever is to move.
From b6 your king controls the squares in front of the pawn, so it can walk all the way to b8.

title: Defending: Hold the Opposition
description: You are defending. Keep your king in front of the pawn and use the opposition to draw.
hint: Stay on the e-file in front of the pawn. When the white king comes to the 6th rank, take the opposition.
technique: Stay directly in front of the pawn
Retreat straight back (to e8), not to the side
When the white king reaches the 6th rank, take the opposition
If the pawn reaches the 7th with check, go to the corner square in front
pitfall: The white king got in front of the pawn onto a key square. Keep your king facing it, and when it comes forward, take the opposition.

lesson.text: Your king belongs **right in front of the pawn**. Stay on the e-file and face the white king.
If the pawn reaches e7 with your king on e8, White can only stalemate you — this is the drawn picture.

title: Rook Pawn: Run to the Corner
description: A rook pawn is the weakest pawn. If the defending king reaches the corner, it can never be driven out.
hint: Keep your king on a8, b8 or nearby; White can only stalemate you.
technique: Get the king into the corner in front of the pawn
Shuffle between a8 and b8/b7
White's only try ends in stalemate
pitfall: Your king left the corner area. Against a rook pawn, stay on a8/b8 and never step away.

lesson.text: A rook pawn is the weakest pawn: once your king reaches the **corner**, it can never be driven out.
Just shuttle between a8 and b8. White's best try ends in stalemate.

title: The Square of the Pawn
description: The white king is far away. Can your king catch the passed pawn?
hint: Step diagonally into the square of the pawn: Kg7!
technique: Draw the square from the pawn to its promotion square
If your king can step into the square, it catches the pawn
Diagonal moves are as fast as straight ones
pitfall: Your king stayed outside the square of the pawn and couldn't catch it.

lesson.text: Draw a **square** from the pawn to its promotion square. If your king can step inside, it catches the pawn.
**Kg7!** steps into the square. From there, head straight for the pawn.

title: The Réti Manoeuvre
description: Réti's famous study (1921). The white king seems hopelessly far from both pawns — yet it's a draw!
hint: Kg7! The king chases the h-pawn and approaches c6 at the same time, walking along the diagonal.
technique: A king moving diagonally can pursue two goals at once
Threaten to support your own pawn
Force Black to spend time, then step into the square of the h-pawn
pitfall: Your king chased only one goal. Walk along the diagonal so it chases the h-pawn and supports your c-pawn at the same time.

lesson.text: **Kg7!** — the king walks down the diagonal, chasing the h-pawn **and** heading towards your c-pawn.
A diagonal king walk is as fast as a straight one, so one route does two jobs. Black must choose — and either way it's a draw.

title: The Outside Passed Pawn
description: Your a-pawn is far away from the other pawns. Use it as a decoy to win the kingside pawns.
hint: Push the a-pawn. When the black king runs after it, march your king to the kingside pawns.
technique: The outside passer drags the enemy king away
Your king attacks the pawns left behind
Don't rush to promote if the king is already in the square — use it as a decoy
pitfall: Your king didn't reach the kingside pawns in time. Use the a-pawn as bait, then march your king straight to the other wing.

lesson.text: Your a-pawn is far from the other pawns. Push it: the black king must run over to stop it.
While Black's king is busy on the a-file, **your king feasts** on the kingside pawns.

title: The Pawn Breakthrough
description: Three pawns against three, both kings far away. There is a brilliant way to create a passed pawn.
hint: b6!! — after axb6 c6! or cxb6 a6!, one white pawn promotes.
technique: Sacrifice the middle pawn first
Then sacrifice the second pawn to clear the way
The last pawn runs through
pitfall: The breakthrough only works with your pawns on the 5th rank and the enemy king far away. Start with b6!

lesson.text: **b6!!** — if ...axb6 then c6!, and if ...cxb6 then a6!
One of your pawns breaks through, and the black king on h8 is too far away to stop it.

title: The Wrong Rook Pawn
description: White is a bishop and a pawn up, yet it's a draw: the bishop does not control the h8 promotion square.
hint: Stay in the corner. Shuffle between h8 and g8 (or g7). White can't drive you out without stalemating you.
technique: Rook pawn + bishop of the wrong colour = draw if the defending king reaches the corner
Keep your king on h8/g8/g7
Don't leave the corner
pitfall: Your king left the corner. Against the wrong bishop, the h8 corner is a fortress — stay there.

lesson.text: White's bishop is light-squared, but h8 is a **dark** square. The bishop can never chase your king out of the corner.
Shuttle between h8 and g8 (or g7). White can only stalemate you.

title: The Lucena Position
description: The most important winning rook endgame. Your pawn is on the 7th, your king in front of it, and the enemy king is cut off.
hint: Build a bridge: Rd4!, then bring the king out and block the checks with the rook on the 4th rank.
technique: Lift your rook to the 4th rank (Rd4)
Bring your king out from in front of the pawn
When the checks come, interpose the rook on the b-file (Rb4)
Promote the pawn
pitfall: The checks never stopped or the black king came back. Keep the black king cut off and build the bridge with your rook on the 4th rank.

lesson.text: Your rook cuts the black king off from the pawn. Now **build a bridge**: Rd4!
Step out with your king. When the black rook checks, walk towards your rook and **block the check on the 4th rank**.

title: The Philidor Defence
description: You are a pawn down. Use Philidor's third-rank defence to hold the draw.
hint: Keep your rook on the 6th rank until the pawn advances to e6, then drop it to the 1st rank and check from behind.
technique: Rook on your 3rd rank (here the 6th) stops the king advancing
Keep your king in front of the pawn
When the pawn reaches e6, give checks from behind from the far end
The white king has no shelter
pitfall: Your rook left the 6th rank too early (or too late), letting the white king step in front of the pawn.

lesson.text: **Philidor's defence**: keep your rook on the **6th rank**. The white king can't step forward without walking into checks.
As soon as the pawn moves to e6, it no longer shelters its king: drop your rook to the 1st rank and **check from behind**.

title: The Vancura Position
description: Rook against rook and a-pawn. With the white rook in front of the pawn, the Vancura defence holds: attack the pawn from the side.
hint: Keep your rook on the 6th rank attacking a6 from the side, and your king near g7/h7.
technique: Rook attacks the pawn from the side (from f6)
Your king stays on g7/h7, out of rook checks along the 7th
If the white king comes close, give checks from the side and return to the 6th rank
pitfall: Your rook stopped attacking the pawn from the side. In the Vancura, it stays on the 6th rank until it can check from behind.

lesson.text: White's rook is stuck in front of its pawn. Attack the a6-pawn **from the side** with your rook on the 6th rank.
Keep your king on g7/h7. If the white king comes to protect the pawn, check it from behind.

title: Rook Behind the Passed Pawn
description: Tarrasch's rule: rooks belong behind passed pawns. Your rook supports the a-pawn from behind while Black's rook is stuck passively in front of it.
hint: Black's rook can't leave a7. March your king towards the queenside (or attack the kingside pawns) and Black runs out of moves.
technique: Rook behind your passed pawn
Advance the pawn to tie Black's rook down
Activate your king
pitfall: Your rook or king lost the grip. Keep the rook behind the pawn and use your king to break in while Black is tied up.

lesson.text: **Tarrasch's rule**: rooks belong behind passed pawns. Your rook pushes the a-pawn while Black's rook is stuck in front of it.
Black's rook can't move, so your king walks forward. Soon Black runs out of good moves.

title: Rook vs Pawn
description: A rook usually beats a pawn, but only if your king helps in time. Stop the pawn and win it.
hint: Bring your king towards the pawn at once (Kd2!) and use the rook to stop it from behind or on the b-file.
technique: Rook behind or in front of the pawn's path
Bring your king towards the pawn
Watch out: if the pawn promotes with the enemy king's support, it may be a draw
pitfall: The pawn got too far or your rook was attacked. King first: bring it towards the pawn immediately.

lesson.text: Your king must come back at once: **Kd2!** The rook alone can't stop a pawn supported by its king.
Then use the rook on the b-file to stop the pawn, and win it with your king.

title: Cut Off the King
description: Your rook cuts the black king off along the d-file. Keep it cut off and escort the c-pawn.
hint: Advance the king with the pawn; if Black checks from the side, approach the rook to block.
technique: The cut-off king can't help its rook
King and pawn advance together
Aim for the Lucena position
pitfall: The black king crossed the d-file. Keep the cut-off at all costs.

lesson.text: Your rook on the d-file keeps the black king out of the game. **Never let it cross.**
Walk the pawn up with your king beside it. If Black checks from the side, head towards your rook.

title: Queen vs Pawn on the 7th (Knight Pawn)
description: A pawn on the 7th supported by its king. With a knight pawn (or centre pawn) the queen wins.
hint: Check and attack the pawn so the king must stand in front of it. Each time, bring your king one step closer.
technique: Force the enemy king in front of its pawn with checks
That gives you a free tempo to bring your king closer
Repeat until your king helps capture the pawn or mate
pitfall: The pawn promoted or slipped away. Check until the king stands in front of its pawn, then step closer with your king.

lesson.text: Check and attack the pawn until the black king has to stand **in front of it** on b1.
Each time the king blocks its own pawn, you get a free move: bring your king one step closer. Repeat.

title: Triangulation as Black (Alburt–Kasparov 1978)
description: Kasparov, playing Black, won this ending by triangulating. White's king can only shuttle between f1, g1 and f2.
hint: ...Kf5! Kg1 Ke5! — your king reaches e4 again with White to move.
technique: Find the zugzwang position (Black king on e4, White to move)
Lose a tempo with a king triangle f5–e5–e4
Then invade via f4 and g3 to win the h3 pawn
pitfall: You didn't lose the tempo. Reach this same position with White to move — then White is in zugzwang.

lesson.text: This is **mutual zugzwang**: whoever has to move loses ground. Lose a tempo with a triangle: ...Kf5, ...Ke5, ...Ke4.
White's king can only shuttle, so it can't copy you. Once White must give way, your king walks in and the f-pawn promotes.

title: Rook Triangulation (Topalov–Karpov 2002)
description: Even rooks can lose a tempo. White uses checks to return to the same position with Black to move.
hint: Rh7+ Kd8 Rh8+ Kd7 Rh6 — now Black is in zugzwang.
technique: Give two checks that return the rook to h6
Black's king must step away from the pawn
Then free your king with Ka7 and promote
pitfall: Your king stayed stuck in front of the pawn. Lose a tempo with rook checks so Black has to move in this position.

lesson.text: With Black to move here, Black would lose. Use checks to come back with Black to move: **Rh7+ Kd8 Rh8+ Kd7 Rh6**.
In zugzwang, Black's rook or king must give way, and your pawn promotes.

title: Triangulation
description: With Black to move this position is lost for Black — but it's White to move. Lose a tempo with the king so Black ends up in zugzwang.
hint: Ke5! Kc6 Kd4! Kd7 Kd5 — the king walks around a triangle while Black's king can only shuttle between two squares.
technique: Recognise the mutual zugzwang
Walk your king around a triangle of three squares
Return to the same position with the opponent to move
Then invade with Ke6–d6–e7–d7
pitfall: You handed Black the move in the critical position. Triangulate: Ke5, Kd4, Kd5.

lesson.text: With Black to move this would be lost for Black. Walk your king around a **triangle** — e5, d4, d5 — and come back with Black to move.
Black's king can only shuttle between two squares, so it can't copy your triangle. Then your king breaks in.

title: King and Pawn from the Start
description: Even with the pawn on its starting square, White wins — if the king leads the way.
hint: Kd2 or Kf2 first — the king must lead the way. Pushing the pawn too early lets Black take the opposition.
technique: King first, pawn later
Aim for the key squares d4, e4 and f4
Use the pawn's one-or-two step choice to win the opposition
pitfall: You pushed the pawn too early and the black king took the opposition in front of it.

lesson.text: **King first!** Your king must lead the way: Kd2 or Kf2, then up the board in front of the pawn.
Reach a key square (d4, e4 or f4) before you push the pawn.

title: Two Pawns vs King
description: Two pawns are usually an easy win. Advance them together, supported by your king.
hint: Bring the king up first; pawns side by side defend each other.
technique: Pawns side by side control the squares in front of them
If the king attacks one pawn, push the other
Use your king to escort them
pitfall: A pawn was lost. Keep the pawns together so they protect each other, and bring your king to help.

lesson.text: Bring your king up first — pawns go faster with an escort.
Advance the pawns together. If the black king attacks one, push the other so they defend each other.

title: Rook Pawn with the Right Bishop
description: Here the bishop controls the dark h8 promotion square, so the rook pawn wins. Beware of stalemate!
hint: Cover g8/g7 with the bishop before pushing the pawn to h7.
technique: The bishop must control the queening square
Don't stalemate the king in the corner
Push h7 with check at the right moment
pitfall: Stalemate or a lost pawn. Cover g8/g7 with the bishop first, and always leave the black king a move.

lesson.text: Your bishop controls the **dark** h8 square, so this rook pawn wins.
Beware of stalemate: never leave the black king without a move while it's not in check.

title: Knight and Pawn vs King
description: Knight and pawn win easily if the pawn is protected and the king supports it.
hint: Bring the king in front of the pawn; use the knight to keep the black king away.
technique: Protect the pawn with the king or knight
King in front of the pawn
Knight checks gain tempi
pitfall: The pawn was lost or the black king blocked it. Keep the pawn protected and lead with your king.

lesson.text: Keep the pawn protected: the knight and pawn guard each other so the black king can't grab anything.
Bring your king in front of the pawn, then push it, using the knight to take squares away.

title: Rook vs Bishop: The Right Corner
description: Rook against bishop is usually a draw. Keep your king in the corner the bishop does NOT control (h8 is dark, your bishop is light).
hint: Stay in the h8 corner and use the bishop to block checks on g8 or h7.
technique: The safe corner is the one of the opposite colour to your bishop
Block rook checks with the bishop
Avoid the corner of your bishop's colour — mating nets appear there
pitfall: Your king went to the wrong corner or the bishop got trapped. Stay in the corner the bishop does NOT control.

lesson.text: Your bishop is light-squared, so the **safe corner is the dark one**: h8.
Block checks with the bishop on g8 or h7 — in the right corner, that never loses the bishop.

title: Rook vs Knight: Stay Together
description: Rook against knight is a draw if the knight stays close to its king. A lone knight far away gets trapped.
hint: Bring the knight back towards your king (Nh3–f4 or Ng4), and keep the king in the centre.
technique: Keep the knight next to the king
Stay away from the corners
Don't let the knight get cut off
pitfall: The knight got separated from its king and was trapped. Keep it close.

lesson.text: Your knight is far from its king and the white king is close to it. Bring it home: **...Nd3+**.
Knight next to king = draw. A lone knight far from its king can be trapped.

title: Queen vs Central Pawn
description: Black's pawn is about to promote, but against a centre pawn the queen wins with checks and pins.
hint: Check the king until it has to stand in front of the pawn, then bring your king closer.
technique: Approach with checks and queen moves that attack the pawn
Each time the king blocks the pawn, use the tempo to bring your king
Finish by winning the pawn or with mate
pitfall: The pawn promoted. Check until the king stands in front of its pawn, then bring your king closer.

lesson.text: Use checks and pins to force the black king in front of its pawn on **d1**.
Every time the king blocks the pawn, use the free move to bring your king one step closer.

title: Queen vs Pawn: The Staircase
description: The black king supports a knight pawn on b2. Stop it and win.
hint: Keep the pawn under control with the queen (Qb1 blocks it for good) and march your king over.
technique: Control the queening square
Bring your king to help
Don't allow a stalemate in the corner
pitfall: The pawn promoted. Blockade the promotion square with your queen, then bring your king.

lesson.text: **Qb1!** blockades the pawn for good.
With the pawn stopped, march your king over and pick it up.

title: Distant Opposition
description: The white king wants to get ahead of its pawn. Only one move stops it: take the opposition from far away.
hint: Kd7! — same file as the white king, with three squares between you.
technique: Kings on the same file with an odd number of squares between them
Mirror the white king as it approaches
Distant opposition turns into direct opposition
pitfall: The white king got past you. Mirror its moves: same file, odd number of squares between the kings.

lesson.text: Opposition also works **from far away**: kings on the same file with an odd number of squares between them (3 or 5).
Keep mirroring the white king. As it comes closer, the distant opposition becomes the normal opposition — and White can't get through.

title: Diagonal Opposition
description: The kings are far apart. Only one move wins: take the opposition along the diagonal.
hint: Kc3! — on the same diagonal as the black king with an odd number of squares between.
technique: Opposition also works on diagonals
Keep the opposition as the kings come closer
Reach a key square in front of your pawn (d5, e5, f5)
pitfall: You lost the opposition and the black king blocked your pawn.

lesson.text: **Diagonal opposition**: kings on the same diagonal with an odd number of squares between them. **Kc3!** faces the g7 king.
Keep the opposition as the kings approach, and reach a key square: d5, e5 or f5.

title: The Rule of the Square
description: Your king is far away, but so is Black's. Can your pawn run home on its own?
hint: b5! — push at once, before the black king steps into the square.
technique: Draw the square from the pawn to its promotion rank
If the enemy king can't step inside, the pawn promotes alone
Every pawn push makes the square smaller
pitfall: You gave the black king time to step into the square of the pawn.

lesson.text: **The rule of the square**: draw a square from your pawn to the 8th rank. Black's king on g5 is just outside it.
**b5!** makes the square smaller at once, and the black king can never catch up.

title: Queen vs Bishop Pawn: Stalemate Trick
description: You are defending with a c-pawn on the 7th. With the white king far away, a stalemate trick saves you.
hint: Stay near the pawn: Kc1 or Kd1. When the queen blocks c1, run to a1 — taking the pawn is stalemate.
technique: Keep your king next to the pawn
When the queen blockades, go to the corner a1
Qxc2 would then be stalemate
pitfall: Your king walked away from the pawn. With a bishop pawn, stay near c1/b1/a1 so the stalemate trick works.

lesson.text: Here Black's king sits in the corner. If the queen takes the pawn on c2, it's **stalemate**!
So stay next to the pawn and keep threatening to promote. The white king is too far away to help.

title: Queen vs Rook Pawn: The Corner Fortress
description: You have an a-pawn on the 7th. With the white king far away, hide in the corner and it's a draw.
hint: Kb2! — stay next to the pawn. If you are driven to a1, White must free you or it's stalemate.
technique: Stay next to the pawn (b1, b2)
Your king in front of the pawn on a1 is stalemate-proof
The white king is too far to help
pitfall: You left the corner area. With a rook pawn on the 7th, keep your king on b1, b2 or a1.

lesson.text: Against a rook pawn the corner is your friend: with your king on a1 in front of the pawn, Black has no moves — **stalemate**.
**Kb2!** keeps your king next to the pawn. The white king is too far away to help its queen.
